candidates.title: TwinQuant: Learnable Subspace Decomposition for 4-Bit LLM Quantization
candidates.abstract: 4-bit quantization reduces the memory footprint and latency of large language model inference, but its aggressive precision reduction can severely degrade accuracy. Prior methods address this by decomposing each weight matrix into two components (e.g., via singular value decomposition) and quantizing them separately, assigning the bulk of values to a low-precision residual component while handling outliers with a high-precision low-rank component. However, such decompositions are designed to minimize the real-valued energy of the residual, rather than the post-quantization error of the residual and low-rank components. We propose TwinQuant, a 4-bit quantization framework that learns quantization-friendly decomposed subspaces and jointly reshapes both the low-rank and residual components. TwinQuant learns component-specific transformations via a joint optimization over the Stiefel and general linear manifolds, flattening their distributions and reducing dynamic-range imbalance. To enable efficient end-to-end execution, we further design a fused dual-component kernel that pipelines the two-stage low-rank computation on-chip and merges both components with a single epilogue, avoiding intermediate global-memory traffic. Across LLaMA3 and Qwen3 models, TwinQuant preserves near-FP16 accuracy and delivers up to $1.8\times$ end-to-end speedup over an FP16 baseline.
candidates.reason: TwinQuantは低rank成分と残差成分の量子化後誤差を同時に最適化するためStiefel/一般線形多様体上の変換を学習。dual-componentのfused kernelがon-chipで低rank計算をpipeline化し、global memoryへの中間出力を避ける。LLaMA3/Qwen3でFP16に近い精度を保ちFP16 baseline比最大1.8倍end-to-end高速化と報告。

candidates.title: Advancing SVD-based LLM Compression via Layer-Wise Error Model Search
candidates.abstract: Low-rank SVD-based compression offers a powerful strategy to reduce the computational costs of LLMs. However, existing methods face two key limitations: (i) global rank allocation, where uncalibrated error proxies fail to capture complex error propagation, and (ii) decomposition quality, where Fisher-based estimators suffer from severe rank collapse. In this work, we address these limitations by introducing Layer-wise Error Modeling Search (LEMS) and KFAC-SVD. LEMS advances rank allocation by introducing a layer-wise error surrogate that integrates local and global layer importance alongside a propagation bias, enabling effective global rank allocation via an ILP formulation. KFAC-SVD improves decomposition quality by utilizing token-wise statistics, mitigating the rank deficiency observed in prior Fisher-based SVD approaches. Across Mistral, Qwen3, and Llama 3 model families, we show that LEMS consistently outperforms existing search strategies, delivering significant zero-shot accuracy gains of up to 4.7 p.p. that generalize to model sizes of 70B parameters, while KFAC-SVD achieves an average perplexity improvement of 19%. Project page and code: https://lems-svd.github.io
candidates.reason: LEMSはlayerごとの局所・大域重要度と誤差伝播biasを組み合わせたsurrogateをILPで最適化し、SVD rankを配分する。KFAC-SVDはtoken統計でFisher近似のrank collapseを緩和。Mistral/Qwen3/Llama3系でzero-shot精度最大4.7ポイント、PPL平均19%改善と報告。推論向け重み圧縮だが実測token/sは要旨にない。

candidates.title: ProVe: Proposer-Verifier Decoding
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive (AR) language models by letting a small model draft tokens serially and a large model verify them in parallel. We reverse these roles. Starting from a standard AR checkpoint, we fine-tune the large model into a proposer that predicts a block of future tokens in a single forward pass, then use one additional forward pass to verify the proposed block. This gives ProVe, Proposer-Verifier decoding. The verifier can be a smaller AR model or the proposer itself; the latter gives ProVe-lossless, which reproduces the proposer's greedy AR decoding. Block proposals already provide substantial room for acceleration: with a block size of 16, the proposed block has an average AR-matching prefix of 6.6 tokens on GSM8K. Across six benchmarks with a 32B proposer, ProVe-lossless reaches 2.5x average AR throughput without training a separate draft head. With a small 3B verifier, ProVe reaches 2.7x average throughput at 2.6 accuracy points below AR on the six-task average, providing a controllable tradeoff between speed and accuracy.
candidates.reason: ProVeは通常のsmall-draft/large-verifyを逆転し、large modelを単一forwardで複数tokenを提案するproposerへ微調整する。別のsmall AR verifierかproposer自身で検証でき、後者は元proposerのgreedy AR出力と一致するlossless版。32B proposerの6 benchmarkでlossless平均2.5倍throughput、3B verifier版2.7倍だが平均2.6精度ポイント低下と報告。

candidates.title: ValuSpec: Plug-and-Play Candidate Valuation before Target Verification for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Tree-based speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by verifying multiple candidate branches in parallel. However, in practical serving scenarios, similar requests repeatedly induce overlapping candidate branches. While retrieval-based methods mitigate this by reusing historical drafts, the resulting candidate trees often contain many low-quality branches as the candidate tree grows, which reduces verification efficiency and wastes target-side computation. To address this, we propose ValuSpec, a plug-and-play candidate valuation mechanism that filters low-quality branches from a supplied candidate tree before expensive target-side verification. ValuSpec introduces transfer-based supervision to align filtering with the target model's behavior. A filtering threshold is estimated from the target model's greedy trajectories on a calibration split, without any parameter training. The target model then verifies the filtered tree under the output-identical greedy rule, so accepted tokens are guaranteed to match standard autoregressive decoding exactly. Experimental results on HumanEval, GSM8K, Dolly, and SpecBench show that, in our main evaluation, ValuSpec achieves up to 2.38x end-to-end speedup in retrieval-based tree settings. Furthermore, integrating ValuSpec into the EAGLE-3 dynamic tree framework yields up to 2.78x end-to-end speedup without modifying its tree construction strategy, demonstrating that ValuSpec serves as a generally applicable and plug-and-play candidate valuation module.
candidates.reason: ValuSpecはretrievalベースtree speculative decodingの低品質branchをtarget verification前に選別する。targetのgreedy trajectoryから閾値を較正し、出力一致の検証規則を保持。HumanEval/GSM8K/Dolly/SpecBenchでretrieval tree設定最大2.38倍、EAGLE-3動的treeへ組込時最大2.78倍のend-to-end高速化を報告。

candidates.title: FermiGrad-SVD: An LLM Compression Pipeline with Global Rank Selection and Gauge Fixing
candidates.abstract: Low-rank factorization of weight matrices is a promising approach to compress large language models (LLMs), but its practical effectiveness depends on allocating ranks across layers and efficiently representing the resulting factors. We introduce three complementary methods for improving SVD-based LLM compression. First, FermiGrad formulates global layer-wise rank allocation as a differentiable optimization problem by replacing discrete singular-value truncation with continuous Fermi gates. Because FermiGrad optimizes only rank parameters over precomputed low-rank factors, it avoids repeated activation decompositions and backpropagation through SVD operations. Second, the Targeted Compressor extends FermiGrad with a task-specific objective that directs limited model capacity toward a selected domain. At 60% parameter density for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, SciQ-targeted compression achieves 60% MMLU accuracy, exceeding the reported quantized Dobi-SVD result by 10 percentage points, while deliberately trading performance on unrelated tasks for domain specialization. Third, PivGa provides a lossless secondary compression of low-rank factors by exploiting the gauge freedom in their parametrization. The proposed framework is modular, computationally efficient, and applicable at scale, as demonstrated by compressing Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct to 50% parameter density.
candidates.reason: FermiGradは離散的rank切捨てを連続Fermi gateに置換して全layerのrank配分を微分最適化する。Targeted Compressorは対象タスクへ容量を配分し、PivGaは低rank因子のgauge自由度を使って追加のlossless圧縮を行う。Llama3.3-70Bを50% parameter densityへ圧縮と報告。推論実行速度は要旨で実測されていない。
